Release notes

Sourced from flask's releases.

3.1.3

This is the Flask 3.1.3 security fix release, which fixes a security issue but does not otherwise change behavior and should not result in breaking changes compared to the latest feature release.

PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/Flask/3.1.3/ Changes: https://flask.palletsprojects.com/page/changes/#version-3-1-3

  • The session is marked as accessed for operations that only access the keys but not the values, such as in and len. GHSA-68rp-wp8r-4726

3.1.2

This is the Flask 3.1.2 fix release, which fixes bugs but does not otherwise change behavior and should not result in breaking changes compared to the latest feature release.

PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/Flask/3.1.2/ Changes: https://flask.palletsprojects.com/page/changes/#version-3-1-2 Milestone: https://github.com/pallets/flask/milestone/38?closed=1

  • stream_with_context does not fail inside async views. #5774
  • When using follow_redirects in the test client, the final state of session is correct. #5786
  • Relax type hint for passing bytes IO to send_file. #5776

3.1.1

This is the Flask 3.1.1 fix release, which fixes bugs but does not otherwise change behavior and should not result in breaking changes compared to the latest feature release.

PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/Flask/3.1.1/ Changes: https://flask.palletsprojects.com/en/stable/changes/#version-3-1-1 Milestone https://github.com/pallets/flask/milestone/36?closed=1

  • Fix signing key selection order when key rotation is enabled via SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS. GHSA-4grg-w6v8-c28g
  • Fix type hint for cli_runner.invoke. #5645
  • flask --help loads the app and plugins first to make sure all commands are shown. #5673
  • Mark sans-io base class as being able to handle views that return AsyncIterable. This is not accurate for Flask, but makes typing easier for Quart. #5659

3.1.0

This is the Flask 3.1.0 feature release. A feature release may include new features, remove previously deprecated code, add new deprecations, or introduce potentially breaking changes. We encourage everyone to upgrade, and to use a tool such as pip-tools to pin all dependencies and control upgrades. Test with warnings treated as errors to be able to adapt to deprecation warnings early.

PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/Flask/3.1.0/ Changes: https://flask.palletsprojects.com/en/stable/changes/#version-3-1-0 Milestone: https://github.com/pallets/flask/milestone/33?closed=1

  • Drop support for Python 3.8. #5623
  • Update minimum dependency versions to latest feature releases. Werkzeug >= 3.1, ItsDangerous >= 2.2, Blinker >= 1.9. #5624, #5633
  • Provide a configuration option to control automatic option responses. #5496
  • Flask.open_resource/open_instance_resource and Blueprint.open_resource take an encoding parameter to use when opening in text mode. It defaults to utf-8. #5504

  • Add support for the Partitioned cookie attribute (CHIPS), with the SESSION_COOKIE_PARTITIONED config. #5472
  • -e path takes precedence over default .env and .flaskenv files. load_dotenv loads default files in addition to a path unless load_defaults=False is passed. #5628
  • Support key rotation with the SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS config, a list of old secret keys that can still be used for unsigning. Extensions will need to add support. #5621
  • Fix how setting host_matching=True or subdomain_matching=False interacts with SERVER_NAME. Setting SERVER_NAME no longer restricts requests to only that domain. #5553

Updates `gunicorn` from 21.2.0 to 22.0.0
Release notes

Sourced from gunicorn's releases.

Gunicorn 22.0 has been released

Gunicorn 22.0.0 has been released. This version fix the numerous security vulnerabilities. You're invited to upgrade asap your own installation.

Changes:

22.0.0 - 2024-04-17
===================

    

  • use utime to notify workers liveness
    • 

  • migrate setup to pyproject.toml
    • 

  • fix numerous security vulnerabilities in HTTP parser (closing some request smuggling vectors)
    • 

  • parsing additional requests is no longer attempted past unsupported request framing
    • 

  • on HTTP versions < 1.1 support for chunked transfer is refused (only used in exploits)
    • 

  • requests conflicting configured or passed SCRIPT_NAME now produce a verbose error
    • 

  • Trailer fields are no longer inspected for headers indicating secure scheme
    • 

  • support Python 3.12
    • 



** Breaking changes **


    

  • minimum version is Python 3.7
    • 

  • the limitations on valid characters in the HTTP method have been bounded to Internet Standards
    • 

  • requests specifying unsupported transfer coding (order) are refused by default (rare)
    • 

  • HTTP methods are no longer casefolded by default (IANA method registry contains none affected)
    • 

  • HTTP methods containing the number sign (#) are no longer accepted by default (rare)
    • 

  • HTTP versions < 1.0 or >= 2.0 are no longer accepted by default (rare, only HTTP/1.1 is supported)
    • 

  • HTTP versions consisting of multiple digits or containing a prefix/suffix are no longer accepted
    • 

  • HTTP header field names Gunicorn cannot safely map to variables are silently dropped, as in other software
    • 

  • HTTP headers with empty field name are refused by default (no legitimate use cases, used in exploits)
    • 

  • requests with both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length are refused by default (such a message might indicate an attempt to perform request smuggling)
    • 

  • empty transfer codings are no longer permitted (reportedly seen with really old & broken proxies)
    • 



** SECURITY **


    

  • fix CVE-2024-1135
  1. Documentation is available there: https://docs.gunicorn.org/en/stable/news.html
  2. Packages: https://pypi.org/project/gunicorn/

Multiple GH Actions failures traced to: `gh pr list` transient errors aborting `auto-pr` jobs, and both `auto-pr`/`auto-merge` missing concurrency guards that allowed duplicate PR creation races and redundant merge attempts.

## `auto-pr.yml`

  EXISTING=$(gh pr list --head "$BRANCH" --state open --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
  ```

## `auto-merge.yml`
- Added `concurrency: group: auto-merge-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}` — prevents redundant merge attempts queued by rapid `labeled`/`synchronize` events on the same PR

### Motivation

- Keep Linear issues in sync with repository pull request lifecycle by moving matching issues to the correct team workflow states automatically. 
- Ensure updates are safe and deterministic by resolving issues by identifier and using real team workflow state IDs rather than hardcoded values. 

### Description

- Add a single GitHub Actions workflow at `.github/workflows/linear-pr-sync.yml` that triggers on `pull_request` events (`opened`, `reopened`, `ready_for_review`, `closed`).
- Parse `LAF-123` style identifiers from PR titles using a strict regex and skip silently when no identifier is found. 
- Query the Linear GraphQL API to resolve the issue by identifier, load the issue's team workflow states, prefer matching by `type` (`started`/`completed`) and fall back to state `name` (`In Progress`/`Done`), then update the issue state by ID. 
- Only treat `closed` events when `merged == true` as `Done` and treat `opened`/`reopened`/`ready_for_review` as `In Progress`, and use the repository secret `LINEAR_API_KEY` for authentication. 

### Testing

- Verified the workflow YAML parses successfully with `ruby -e "require 'yaml'; YAML.load_file('.github/workflows/linear-pr-sync.yml')"` which printed `YAML OK`. 
- Confirmed that `python3`-embedded script path and logic were exercised locally during development, and noted `PyYAML` is not installed in the sandbox so a Python YAML load check was skipped (environment limitation). 
- Committed the workflow with `git commit` and prepared PR metadata using the repository `make_pr` helper; commit succeeded and file was added to the branch.

Automatically merge eligible PRs once checks pass and pause merging when agents request changes.

- **Review feedback handling**: New `review-response.yml` removes `auto-merge`, adds `review-required`, and posts an acknowledgment comment when another agent submits comments/changes requested.

```bash
# Auto-merge activation via label
gh pr edit <pr> --add-label auto-merge

# Review response effect
# - removes auto-merge
# - adds review-required
# - comments with review link
```

Release notes

Sourced from actions/upload-artifact's releases.

v7.0.0

v7 What's new

Direct Uploads

Adds support for uploading single files directly (unzipped). Callers can set the new archive parameter to false to skip zipping the file during upload. Right now, we only support single files. The action will fail if the glob passed resolves to multiple files. The name parameter is also ignored with this setting. Instead, the name of the artifact will be the name of the uploaded file.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

What's Changed

Full Changelog: https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/compare/v6...v7.0.0

[!IMPORTANT] actions/upload-artifact@v6 now runs on Node.js 24 (runs.using: node24) and requires a minimum Actions Runner version of 2.327.1. If you are using self-hosted runners, ensure they are updated before upgrading.

Node.js 24

This release updates the runtime to Node.js 24. v5 had preliminary support for Node.js 24, however this action was by default still running on Node.js 20. Now this action by default will run on Node.js 24.

- name: Upload CSV as artifact

The auto-pr workflow was failing silently with 0 jobs executed due to a YAML parser error on line 86. The heredoc containing markdown bold syntax (`**Risk tier:**`) was being interpreted as a YAML alias anchor (`*` prefix), causing the parser to reject the entire workflow before job execution.

## Changes

- Replaced heredoc-based PR body construction with `printf` to avoid YAML parser conflicts
- Removed escape sequences (`\``) that were contributing to parsing ambiguity
- Verified all 11 workflow files pass YAML validation

## Before

```yaml
BODY=$(cat <<EOF
**Risk tier:** \`$TIER\`
**Label:** \`$LABEL\`
EOF
)
```

## After

```yaml
printf -v BODY '%s\n\n%s\n%s\n\n%s\n%s' \
  '## Auto-generated PR' \
  '**Risk tier:**' "\`$TIER\`" \
  '**Label:**' "\`$LABEL\`"
```

Workflows will now execute normally instead of failing at parse time.

GitHub Actions workflows had classic expression-injection and word-splitting vulnerabilities; `sanitize_text()` had incomplete YAML escaping that could corrupt frontmatter or cause parse errors.

## Workflow: expression injection → `env:` isolation

`${{ github.event.inputs.* }}`, `${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}`, and `${{ steps.classify.outputs.tier }}` were interpolated directly into `run:` shell bodies — string-substituted before shell parsing, making them injection vectors.

**Fix:** move all untrusted expressions into `env:` blocks so they're passed as environment variables, not raw shell text. Affected workflows: `wayback-audit.yml`, `branch-cleanup.yml`, `auto-pr.yml`.

## Workflow: unquoted `$ARGS` → bash array

`idaho-leg-scraper.yml` built a string `ARGS` and expanded it unquoted (`python3 script.py $ARGS`), subject to shell word-splitting if `$BILL` contained spaces or metacharacters.

```bash
# Before
ARGS="--year $YEAR"
[ -n "$BILL" ] && ARGS="$ARGS --bill $BILL"
python3 idaho_leg_scraper.py $ARGS   # unquoted — word-splits

# After
ARGS=("--year" "$YEAR")
[ -n "$BILL" ] && ARGS+=("--bill" "$BILL")
python3 idaho_leg_scraper.py "${ARGS[@]}"   # array — safe
```

## Scraper: incomplete YAML backslash escaping

`sanitize_text(for_yaml=True)` only escaped `"` → `\"` but not `\`. Scraped content containing `\n`, `\t`, or any `\x` sequence would be interpreted as YAML escape sequences, causing parse errors or silent value corruption in frontmatter.

```python
# Before
text = text.replace('"', '\\"')

# After — backslash must come first
text = text.replace("\\", "\\\\")
text = text.replace('"', '\\"')
```

The Idaho Legislature scraper was failing silently with `"Empty bill list — cannot continue"` and no indication of root cause. This makes remote triage in GitHub Actions logs nearly impossible.

## Changes

### `idaho_leg_scraper.py`

**`get_bill_list()` — diagnostic logging at failure points**
- Network fetch failure now logs the full minidata URL and notes retries are exhausted (previously just `"Could not fetch minidata page"`)
- Fallback soup fetch refactored from nested anonymous call to named `fallback_soup` variable
- When no bill table found on either page, logs minidata page length + first 200 chars at `DEBUG` level (visible with `--verbose`), exposing bot-blocks, redirects, or layout changes

**`main()` — catch uncaught exceptions from `scrape_bills()`**
```python
try:
    new, updated, unchanged, errors = scrape_bills(...)
except Exception as exc:
    log.exception("Unexpected error during scrape: %s", exc)
    return 1
